definitions.explanation: A house provided at public expense to a high-ranking official — a prime minister, governor, mayor, or ambassador — for the duration of the post. The occupant lives there but does not own it.

examples.japanese: {知事|ちじ}は{公邸|こうてい}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: The governor lives in the official residence.

examples.japanese: {首相|しゅしょう}{公邸|こうてい}で{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}が{開|ひら}かれた。
examples.english: A press conference was held at the prime minister's official residence.

examples.japanese: {大使|たいし}{公邸|こうてい}の{夕食|ゆうしょく}{会|かい}に{招|まね}かれ、{各国|かっこく}から{来|き}た{来賓|らいひん}と{話|はな}す{機会|きかい}があった。
examples.english: I was invited to a dinner at the ambassador's official residence and had a chance to talk with guests from various countries.

notes:
Formed from {公|こう} (public) + {邸|てい} (mansion, residence). Usually appears attached to the title of the post: {首相|しゅしょう}{公邸|こうてい}, {知事|ちじ}{公邸|こうてい}, {大使|たいし}{公邸|こうてい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公邸|こうてい}に{入|はい}る: to move into the official residence
- {公邸|こうてい}を{出|で}る: to leave the official residence
- {公邸|こうてい}で{会談|かいだん}する: to hold talks at the official residence

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {私邸|してい}: private residence — the official's own home, contrasted directly with {公邸|こうてい}
- {官邸|かんてい}: official residence and office — for the prime minister, {官邸|かんてい} is the working headquarters, {公邸|こうてい} the living quarters
- {官舎|かんしゃ}: government housing — ordinary housing for civil servants, not a mark of high rank
